steps.do: Create the theme directory for the chart tokens.
Copy the starter token template into the theme directory.
Set the title_sgr token to the bold SGR code 1 in the file.
Set the axis_sgr token to the dim SGR code 2 in the file.
Check that the token file parses as valid JSON.
Run the token tests and confirm they pass.

K-021502.example: After the sed edits, theme/tokens.json holds "title_sgr": "1" and "axis_sgr": "2". The chart renders its title bold and its axis labels dim without literal escape codes in src/chart.py.
K-021502.check: python3 -m json.tool prints the JSON with exit code 0, and pytest reports 3 passed with no failures.
traps: Small models often leave the placeholder TITLE_SGR in place, so run the json.tool check after every sed edit.
Do not hard-code escape codes in chart.py. Read them from the token file so the theme changes in one place.
SGR codes are plain numbers like 1 and 2, not the full escape sequence with ESC and bracket.

steps.do: Create the source and test directories for the bar code.
Write src/bars.py with a function that maps a fraction from 0.0 to 1.0 to one of nine glyphs: space, then ▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█.
Write tests/test_bars.py asserting that 0.0 gives a space, 1.0 gives █, and 0.5 gives ▄.
Run the bar tests.
Print the eight-step ramp to confirm the glyphs render one cell wide.
Confirm the ramp has eight glyphs by counting its characters.

K-021503.example: A value of 0.5 in a 10-row bar chart fills 5 full cells, and the top cell uses ▄ for half height. The printed ramp shows eight distinct block heights from ▁ to █.
K-021503.check: pytest reports 3 passed, and the python3 length command prints 8.
traps: Small models often fill every bar cell with █, which throws away the eighth-cell precision the glyph set provides.
Check that a value of 1.0 maps to █ and not to an index past the end of the list.
Do not count bytes. Each glyph is multi-byte in UTF-8 but occupies one terminal cell.

steps.do: Check how many colors the current terminal supports.
Create the source directory for the chart code.
In src/chart.py, return no style when the NO_COLOR variable is set to any non-empty value, use truecolor when COLORTERM is truecolor, and otherwise use the 256-color form.
Render the demo chart with NO_COLOR set and pipe it through cat -v to reveal any escape bytes.
Run the color tests.

K-021504.example: With NO_COLOR=1, the demo output contains no ^[ sequences in the cat -v view. With tput colors printing 256, each series uses the 38;5;N form.
K-021504.check: tput colors prints 256 or more, the cat -v output contains zero ^[ sequences, and pytest reports all tests passed.
traps: Small models often treat NO_COLOR as a boolean and ignore its value. Per no-color.org, any non-empty value turns color off.
Write the escape byte as \e or \x1b in code. A literal backslash followed by e is plain text and renders nothing.
Do not assume 256 colors. Read tput colors first, since a basic terminal may report only 8.

They skip the dark background check.

Confirm the test log names the light, dark, and accessibility3 variants.

K-021726.check: find lists 9 PNG paths, and xcodebuild ends with ** TEST SUCCEEDED **.

A snapshot that is not rerun after a token change still passes against a stale reference.

steps.do: Check the current min-height and min-width values in the library styles.

K-021729.check: grep -c prints a number of 3 or more, and rg prints the existing aria attributes in src/lib.

Confirm the token file defines the list type scale.

K-021730.example: The file src/components/List/List.tsx line 14 uses text-[13px], so the first search prints that line and the card fails until the class becomes text-list-item. After the fix, the search prints nothing and the unit test prints Tests: 3 passed.

Write down the measured contrast ratio of body text against the row background.

K-021731.check: axe prints 0 violations for color-contrast, and the Playwright test prints 1 passed.

Check hover and zebra rows, not only the default row.

Confirm the built rule sets font-size to 0.875rem.

K-021732.check: npm run build exits 0, the search finds one .text-list-item rule with font-size:.875rem, and Playwright prints 1 passed.

Unknown classes compile without an error and are silently dropped, so check the built CSS.
Check the output file, not only the source.

Start the preview server for the production build.
Run the computed-style test for list items.
List the tests in the spec to confirm the expected count.
Write down the computed font size in px for one list item.

K-021733.check: Playwright prints 0 failed in the line reporter, and the list command shows the expected test count.

Start the preview build first, or the test runs against a stale server.
Compare the computed value in px, not the class name.

steps.do: Build the production bundle for the app.
Serve the built bundle on port 4173.
Run Lighthouse with the accessibility category only and save the JSON report.
Read the accessibility score from the JSON report.
Fail the change if the score is below 1.

K-021734.example: A printed score of 0.96 means one audit failed, such as color-contrast on the row count label. Open the report and find the failed audit id under audits before editing the classes.
K-021734.check: jq prints 1, and any value below 1 means at least one accessibility audit failed.

Do not run Lighthouse against the dev server, because it adds noise to the results.
Do not commit the reports folder without reading the file first.

steps.do: Find the dark theme token overrides.
Run the axe WCAG AA check with the dark theme enabled.
Run the Playwright test that screenshots and measures light and dark list rows.
Count the dark variant classes in the list component.
Compare the dark variant count with the list item count and record the result.

K-021735.example: Dark row text uses dark:text-slate-300 (#cbd5e1) on dark:bg-slate-900 (#0f172a), which gives about 12.0:1 and passes. A row missing its dark: class falls back to the light color and must be counted as a failure.
K-021735.check: axe prints 0 violations, Playwright prints 2 passed for light and dark, and rg -c prints a count equal to the number of list item classes.

Confirm the dark mode strategy in the Tailwind config, because dark: variants depend on it.

steps.do: Create the output folder for the build.
Build and minify the Tailwind CSS from the input file, scanning the content globs in the config.
Measure the byte size of the built CSS file.
Confirm a chart utility used in the components was compiled into the output.

K-021736.example: The build prints no errors, and wc reports 14832 bytes for ./dist/chart.css, under the 20000-byte budget. grep -c returns 1, so the tabular-nums utility is present.
K-021736.check: wc -c prints a number at or below 20000, and grep -c prints 1 or more. If the byte count is over 20000, reduce the content globs or remove unused arbitrary values.
traps: A small model may skip the minify flag, so the size check measures the wrong file. Always pass --minify.

steps.do: List the chart source files so you know which files to scan.
Search the chart folder for template literal syntax that builds class names at runtime.
Build the CSS from the input file so the output reflects the current source.
Confirm that a literal fill color used by the chart is present in the built CSS.

K-021737.example: The grep for template syntax prints lines such as src/components/chart/Bar.tsx:12 with the bg-${tone}-500 pattern, which must be replaced by a lookup table of full class strings. After the fix, the second grep prints no lines, and grep -c returns 1 for fill-emerald-500.
K-021737.check: grep -rnF '${' prints no class-name lines in the chart folder, and grep -c prints 1 for each literal class the chart uses. Any dynamic class found in the first search is a failure.

Building a class from parts like 'fill-' plus a variable is invisible to Tailwind, and the class silently does nothing. Use a map of complete class names.

steps.do: Create the reports folder for the Lighthouse output.
Run Lighthouse against the running chart page, limited to the performance category, and save JSON.
Read the performance score from the JSON report.

K-021738.example: Lighthouse finishes and writes ./reports/chart-lh.json for the chart page served at localhost:3000. jq prints 0.93, which is above the 0.90 gate.
K-021738.check: jq prints a number of 0.90 or higher. A value below 0.90 means the chart page fails the gate, so inspect the largest contentful paint and total blocking time in the report.

K-021741.check: xcodebuild -list prints a Schemes section, and the plan lists 6 snapshot cases.

steps.do: Create the spec file tests/chart-render.spec.ts, then write a test that navigates to the chart page, starts a timer with Date.now() after navigation completes, waits for locator('svg path').first() to be visible, stops the timer, and asserts the elapsed time is below 200 milliseconds.
Confirm the spec file exists before running it.
Run only that spec with the line reporter so the timing result prints.

K-021742.example: The spec measures Date.now() after page.goto completes and again after locator('svg path').first() becomes visible, then calls expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(200). The run prints 1 passed with an elapsed time of 146 milliseconds.
K-021742.check: The output ends with '1 passed'. If it prints an assertion error showing a value above 200, the chart render exceeds budget.
traps: A small model may time the whole page load instead of the chart, so the budget fails for unrelated images. Start the timer after navigation and wait for the svg path.
Playwright needs a configured baseURL or a full URL in page.goto. Without one the test fails before it measures anything.

steps.do: Create the spec file tests/chart-resize.spec.ts, then write a test that opens a Chromium CDP session, calls Performance.enable, reads LayoutCount, resizes the viewport five times while waiting for requestAnimationFrame after each resize, reads LayoutCount again, and asserts the delta is below 5.
Confirm the spec file exists before running it.
Run that spec to get the layout count result.

K-021743.example: Before resizing, LayoutCount is 212, and after five viewport changes it is 214, so the delta of 2 is below the limit of 5. The run prints 1 passed.
K-021743.check: The output shows '1 passed', and the asserted delta is 4 or lower. A delta of 5 or more means the chart is forcing layout on each resize step.
traps: A small model may read LayoutCount without enabling the Performance domain first, so the value stays at zero and the test passes wrongly. Call Performance.enable before the first read.
Resizing the viewport without waiting for the ResizeObserver callback counts the wrong frame. Wait for requestAnimationFrame before the second read.

steps.do: Create the spec file tests/chart-motion.spec.ts, then write a test that sets reducedMotion to reduce in the browser context, loads the chart, and asserts the chart root computed contain value is paint and its computed animation-duration and transition-duration are both 0s.
Confirm the spec file exists before running it.
Run that spec to confirm the containment and motion styles are applied.

K-021744.example: The chart root has the class contain-paint and motion-reduce:transition-none, so getComputedStyle reports contain as paint and transition-duration as 0s. The run prints 1 passed.
K-021744.check: The output shows '1 passed', and the asserted computed values are paint and 0s. A value of none or a nonzero duration means the utility is missing or overridden.
traps: A small model may check the class name in the markup and skip the computed style, but the class can be overridden. Assert the computed style in the browser.
The motion-reduce variant needs prefers-reduced-motion emulation, or the reduced-motion branch never runs. Set reducedMotion to reduce in the test context.

steps.do: Read the installed Tailwind version from the dependency tree.
Search the stylesheets for a v4 custom dark variant.
Search the config file for a v3 darkMode setting.
Choose the class strategy if the app has a theme toggle, otherwise choose the media strategy.
Write the chosen setting and the file that holds it into the plan.

K-021745.example: npm ls prints tailwindcss@4.1.0 and the search finds no custom-variant line, so the plan adds a custom dark variant that matches the .dark class to src/app.css. The toggle exists, so the strategy is class, not media.
K-021745.check: The version line starts with tailwindcss@4 or tailwindcss@3, and the plan names one strategy and one file.
traps: Small models write v3 darkMode config into a v4 project, which has no effect. Check the version first.
Choosing media when the app has a toggle breaks the user's manual choice. Pick class in that case.

steps.do: Read the existing theme variables in the global stylesheet.
Search the chart folder for Tailwind gray scale classes to see what is already in use.
List eight chart tokens: grid, axis label, tooltip background, tooltip text, and series 1 to 4.
Set each text token to at least 4.5:1 against its background and each graphic token to at least 3:1.
Write the light and dark value for each token in the plan table.

K-021746.example: The grid token is slate-200 in light mode and slate-700 in dark mode, and the axis label is slate-600 on white, which must reach 4.5:1. The plan lists eight rows with a light and dark value in each.
K-021746.check: The plan table has 8 token rows, each with a light value and a dark value, and each text row states a ratio of at least 4.5:1.

steps.do: List files that mention Tooltip or Legend in the source.
Search the chart folder for hardcoded white backgrounds.
Write a surface pair for each overlay, with a background, a border, and a text class for each mode.
State the target contrast of at least 4.5:1 for each text pair so the verify stage can test it.

K-021747.example: The search finds Tooltip in src/charts/Tooltip.tsx, which uses bg-white. The plan pairs it with dark:bg-slate-900 and dark:border-slate-700, and the text pair must reach 4.5:1.
K-021747.check: The plan lists one surface pair per overlay, and each text pair has a stated target of at least 4.5:1.

steps.do: Install the form, schema, and resolver packages in the project.
Create src/components/RoleSelect.tsx that calls useForm and gets register and handleSubmit from its return value.
Spread register('role', { required: 'Choose a role' }) onto a select element whose first option has value '' and text 'Pick one'.

K-021748.check: npx tsc --noEmit exits with code 0 and prints no errors, and submitting the placeholder shows the text 'Choose a role' under the select.

steps.do: Create src/components/PlanSelect.tsx with useState for the value and a useState for the error string.

Check formatting of the component file.

Use useEffect keyed on the parent value to call setValue('city', '') and clear the child options list.
Disable the child select when the parent value is empty so the user cannot pick a city first.

Run ESLint to catch a missing dependency in the useEffect array.
